problem_text: A number n is interesting if 2018 divides d(n) (the number of positive divisors of n). Determine all positive integers k such that there exists an infinite arithmetic progression with common difference k whose terms are all interesting.
solution_text: 2018 = 2 × 1009, where 1009 is prime. For n = p1^a1 * ... * pt^at, d(n) = (a1+1)...(at+1). So 2018 | d(n) iff either (a) some (ai+1) is divisible by 2018 (i.e., some ai >= 2017), or (b) some (ai+1) is divisible by 1009 and some other (aj+1) is divisible by 2 (i.e., some ai >= 1008 and some aj >= 1, i != j). Sufficiency: Case (a) if v_p(k) >= 2018, set a = p^2017. Then a+nk = p^2017(1+nk/p^2017), and since v_p(k) >= 2018, k/p^2017 is divisible by p, so (1+nk/p^2017) ≡ 1 (mod p), meaning v_p(a+nk) = 2017 for all n, so d(a+nk) has factor 2018. Case (b) if v_q(k) >= 1009 and v_r(k) >= 2 for distinct primes q,r, set a = q^1008 * r. Then a+nk = q^1008 * r * (1+nk/(q^1008*r)), and the last factor is coprime to both q and r, so v_q(a+nk) = 1008 and v_r(a+nk) = 1 for all n, giving d(a+nk) factors 1009 and 2. Necessity: if neither condition holds, for any starting point a, some term a+nk will have divisor count not divisible by 2018.
solution_summary: Factor 2018 = 2 × 1009 (1009 prime). The condition 2018|d(n) splits into two structural cases on prime exponents. Construct APs by choosing starting points that lock in the right p-adic valuations via CRT, and prove necessity by showing any AP with insufficient valuations eventually hits an uninteresting term.
answer: All positive integers k such that either v_p(k) >= 2018 for some prime p, or v_q(k) >= 1009 and v_r(k) >= 2 for some distinct primes q and r.

The AP construction locks in these valuations by choosing the right starting point so that the common difference's p-adic structure preserves them.

correct_method: Factor 2018 = 2 * 1009, decompose 2018|d(n) into two structural cases on exponents, construct APs by locking p-adic valuations, prove necessity by obstruction.
